alt: Chart of the average number of days with measurable rain each month in {city}, {SS} — the wet months that keep materials damp. {summary}

fetch.note: Days with >= 0.10 in. Replaces humidity_monthly: NOAA's normals publish no moisture variable beyond precipitation, so the humidity figures could not have come from the source they cited. This is a rain-frequency measure and the captions describe it as such — it is not a humidity substitute.

captions: {city} sees measurable rain on about {total} days a year, most often in {peak}. Mould needs moisture more than it needs heat, and it is repeated wetting rather than annual totals that keeps materials damp long enough for growth to start.

Rain falls on roughly {total} days a year in {city}, {SS}, peaking in {peak} and easing to {low_value} in {low}. Material that never fully dries between wettings is where growth takes hold, which is why the wet stretches matter more than the dry months.

{city} records measurable rain on about {total} days a year. Frequency is the useful number: a roof, a window seal or a grading fault is tested on every one of those days, and what decides the outcome is whether the material dries out before the next one.
